note: Surveyed multi-agent orchestration over MCP first-hand from 10 primary sources (4.38MB raw bytes banked under mcp-multi-agent.fetch/); an initial 34-quote draft failed 28 of 34 byte checks against the raw page bytes and was rebuilt from disk to 29 verified quotes; 4 vendor doc pages were JS-walled (no quotable prose) and one MCP blog post is dead/404, all recorded as negative findings; no code under mag/ or tools/ touched.

rows.claim: Composition in MCP is host-side fan-out: the host creates one MCP client per server and each client holds a dedicated connection, so cross-server wiring is always the host's job, never server-to-server federation.
rows.quote: The MCP host accomplishes this by creating one MCP client for each MCP server.
rows.steal: One sitting: file watch/inbox/MCP_HOST_PROBE_20261010.md sketching mag's tool broker as a mini-host (one client per server, namespaced registry); no mag/ code until a second MCP server actually lands.
rows.falsifier: The MCP spec or a reference implementation ships server-to-server composition where servers discover and call each other without a host client in the path.

rows.claim: Multi-server hosts kill tool-name collisions with deterministic server-prefixed tool names; the OpenAI Agents SDK ships this as the opt-in include_server_in_tool_names flag.
rows.quote: include_server_in_tool_names is opt-in. When enabled, each local MCP tool is exposed to the model with a deterministic server-prefixed name, which helps avoid collisions when multiple MCP servers publish tools with the same name.
rows.steal: Adopt the same contract in any mag tool aggregation surface: aggregated tool ids get '<server>__<name>' prefixes; register as a named design law when the second server lands.
rows.falsifier: A production multi-server host merges colliding tool names unprefixed and reports zero conflicts or aliasing bugs at scale.

rows.claim: The spec's mitigation list mandates least-privilege per server: sandboxed commands, restricted filesystem and network access, and explicit user grants for anything extra.
rows.quote: Launch MCP servers with restricted access to the file system, network, and other system resources
rows.steal: Spec-before-behavior: write the least-privilege profile requirement into a RIB (memory/rib/RIB_MCP_SANDBOX_<date>.md) before mag ever mounts a third-party MCP server; prose only, one sitting.
rows.falsifier: The spec or a mainstream host recommends sharing one privileged process across all servers with no per-server sandbox.

rows.claim: Local MCP servers are downloaded binaries executed with client privileges on the user's machine, so installing one is binary adoption, not plugin adoption.
rows.quote: Local MCP servers are binaries that are downloaded and executed on the same machine as the MCP client.
rows.steal: Extend the estate's tool-adoption receipt template: every third-party MCP server install files source URL, hash, and consent note in watch/inbox/ before first run.
rows.falsifier: Spec or major hosts auto-install local MCP servers without consent or provenance tracking.

rows.claim: Presenting MCP tools as a filesystem of code APIs collapses context cost: Anthropic's example drops tool-definition tokens from 150,000 to 2,000 and lets the agent compose multiple servers in one code step.
rows.quote: This reduces the token usage from 150,000 tokens to 2,000 tokens
rows.steal: One probe: render the GALA ask/tool manifests as a file tree, have a model write calling code instead of loading every tool def, measure the token delta; receipt in watch/inbox/MCP_TOOLSTREE_20261010.md.
rows.falsifier: A large-scale comparison where code-mode costs more tokens or fails more tasks than direct tool-calls at equal success rates.

rows.claim: Progressive disclosure is the mechanism behind that collapse: models read tool definitions on demand from a filesystem instead of loading them all upfront.
rows.quote: Presenting tools as code on a filesystem allows models to read tool definitions on-demand, rather than reading them all up-front.
rows.steal: Apply on-demand loading to mag's own doc surfaces: point 50-wide drivers at an index file first (corpus_catalog pattern already matches); file the mapping note in watch/inbox.
rows.falsifier: Agents given full upfront tool context outperform filesystem-navigation agents on tool-selection accuracy in controlled evals.

rows.claim: Code-execution agents persist intermediate results as files and resume later: the same residual-plus-leaf law the estate already runs on lanes, now validated by an outside source.
rows.quote: Agents can write intermediate results to files, enabling them to resume work and track progress
rows.steal: No new mechanism: bank as external validation of the incremental lane-file law; add one citing line to docs/DNA.md at its next edit touch.
rows.falsifier: Context-only state persistence demonstrably beats file-based resume on long-horizon agent tasks.

rows.claim: A2A is a separate agent-to-agent layer (web standards, Agent Cards, task delegation) whose opacity principle says agents collaborate without exposing internal state, memory, or tools; it complements rather than replaces MCP.
rows.quote: Operate without exposing their internal state, memory, or tools.
rows.steal: Write an Agent-Card-style manifest spec for mag lanes (lane JSON already carries name, role, IO) and file it in watch/inbox/MCP_A2A_CARD_20261010.md; one sitting.
rows.falsifier: A2A adoption in practice requires agents to share internal memory or plans, contradicting the opacity principle.

rows.claim: The orchestration frameworks converged on one adapter contract: CrewAI aggregates several MCP servers through a single adapter, LangChain's MCPAdapter delegates transport to FastMCP, OpenAI ships MCPServerManager, so the estate can steal the contract without adopting any framework.
rows.quote: Aggregate tools from several MCP servers simultaneously using a single adapter.
rows.steal: Steal the adapter contract only: mag's tool broker speaks 'aggregate N servers behind one adapter object with health-gated connections' per the row-1 design note; no new dependency.
rows.falsifier: A mainstream framework makes agent-to-agent messaging, not server adapters, its primary MCP integration.

rows.claim: Cloudflare's Code Mode pairs tools-as-code with a sandbox: the agent runs in a sandbox that can only reach the tools it is given, with connectivity and authorization handled out of band by MCP.
rows.quote: We'd like the AI agent to run in a sandbox such that it can only access the tools we give it.
rows.steal: If mag ever executes model-written tool code, run it under a restricted profile with a tool allowlist; put the requirement line in the row-1 host probe receipt.
rows.falsifier: Code Mode shipped to production without any sandbox and with no isolation incidents reported.

decision_changed: closed: mcp-orchestration stance - do not adopt an agent framework or MCP fabric now; if mag's tool surface exceeds roughly 50 tools or mounts a third-party MCP server, compose at the host (one client per server, server-prefixed tool names, least-privilege sandbox) with tools-as-code as the scaling path.
